Reference counting works by maintaining a count of references to each object and reclaiming the object when the count drops to zero. However, for objects that reference each other cyclically, the reference count never reaches zero, even if the entire cycle is unreachable from any live part of the program. In contrast, a stop-and-copy garbage collector can identify such cycles as unreachable during its tracing process and will collect the entire cycle properly.
